notes: Title and DOI 10.1109/LWC.2025.3551140 are on p. 1, so the PDF matches. The paper frames its data-aided MIMO channel estimator as reinforcement learning, but nothing is learned from data or experience. p. 3: "the conventional data-driven approach [7] is not applicable to this MDP. To solve the MDP efficiently, a reinforcement learning algorithm in [10] is introduced by approximating the transition and value functions"; the approximations are the most likely transition under correct detection, eq. (21), and "setting η = 0" (p. 3). p. 4: Theorem 1 gives the policy in closed form, α_r(S) = ê_mod/(ê_data + ê_mod), eq. (23), and Algorithm 1 only does "Compute the optimal policy π⋆(S) from (23)" at each time slot. p. 5, Appendix B: "The optimal policy in (23) can be directly derived from (31), whose partial derivative satisfies zero." The only offline step estimates a statistic, not a model (p. 4: "The offline process is applied to estimate initial error variance"). The estimator is therefore a closed-form, decision-directed linear combination of a Gauss-Markov model-based estimate and a data-aided LMMSE estimate; learning appears only as framing and in the baseline RL-LMMSE [8] (p. 4). Borderline because the title says learning-based: if the reviewer counts this MDP solution as learned, it would be area 2 (channel estimation, NMSE and FER) with q1 0 (Rayleigh fading with first-order Gauss-Markov evolution, pp. 1-2), q2 0 (nothing trained; only zeta = 1e-3 and 1e-2), q3 1 (Conv. LMMSE and RL-LMMSE [8] on FER, p. 4), q4 1 (FLOPs and complexity order O(6Ntx^2 Nd + 19Ntx^3), pp. 4-5), q5 0 (no code or data released).
